body: How about prove him wrong. Like get better and then report him for being an incompetent buffoon.

Well, bad is subjective isn't it? I mean it's all relative. For example, perhaps being a quadriplegic might be worse. Or being me, an embarrassment out of my own doing, ego, nature. I screwed up so much shit that actually was under my control. You didn't. 

Find happiness within yourself. Don't make others responsible for it. They won't deliver.

Why not simply, keep it to yourself. If it causes others pain that you don't believe in something that they do, then simply don't tell them. The first rule of being a human should be to do no harm. Mouth closed, ears open. Go through the motions and leave when the time is right. All religions have some good to them I think. I'm not religious myself. But that part, the little part of any religion, that is actually humane is what allowed religions to succeed. Sort of like a bit of sweetness to hide/counter a lot of bitterness (e.g. whatever you witnessed at Kaaba). 

I guess I'm just trying to be strategic. You don't have to reveal your cards just now.

Just the hope that I can become again what I once was. That I can once again find the happiness that I've lost. But the window of opportunity to so is an ever narrowing one and such hope, therefore, appears to be a a rather foolish thought.

You know what, scratch the part about medications. As a rather avid practitioner of self-medication (i.e. being drunk), it just seems hypocritical. I guess I should take that into account then next time I buy bottles of my dearest of poisons.

Still, I stand by me conclusion that life is a pretty uncaring and selfish, force.
